findings.assertion: The Crown's tobacco monopoly and the 20 April 1776 royal approval for a dedicated Mexico City tobacco-factory building preceded construction at today's La Ciudadela by more than a decade; distinguish royal fiscal policy from the later surviving building.
findings.source_locator: La Jornada 20 July 2014 lines 31-32; INAH Mediateca guide indexed '1766' and '20 April 1776', original royal order unexamined.
findings.limitations: The 1776 decree and monopoly law text not inspected; numerical fiscal receipts not established.

findings.assertion: Linda Arnold's edition of a mid-1790s AGN expediente concerns women tobacco workers seeking supervision or schooling for their daughters, while the Crown had an interest in maintaining productive labor; the record documents worker priorities as well as state administration.
geographies: Mexico City / tobacco work; original factory site unresolved
findings.source_locator: AGN Boletín vol 4 no 07 (1996) pp.63-180 abstract, esp. mid-1790s school/guardería description.
findings.limitations: Crucial chronology: women's workplace in the 1790s cannot automatically be placed inside the La Ciudadela building completed in 1807; archival transcription and workplace address unexamined.

findings.assertion: The surviving La Ciudadela complex was built 1793–1807 for the Real Fábrica de Tabacos; published institutional accounts name Antonio González Velázquez, military engineer Miguel Constanzó, and completion by Ignacio Castera, but individual design-stage responsibilities await drawings.
findings.source_locator: INAH catalog ficha 12486 historical description (indexed); La Jornada 20 July 2014 lines 31-32; Arquine 31 July 2012 lines 20-22.
findings.limitations: Do not present one architect as sole designer; original approved drawings and chronology of interruptions not viewed. Current visible materials not surveyed.

findings.assertion: Ángeles González Gamio reports that the Gazeta de México (1807) described twelve fountains and seventeen tobacco-drying patios within La Ciudadela, whose industrial rooms were organized for processing; this is a secondary account of an uninspected period primary description.
geographies: La Ciudadela / original factory courtyard system
findings.source_locator: La Jornada 20 July 2014 line 32 citing Gazeta de México 1807; Arquine 2012 lines 22-24 discusses 2011 plan and four main courtyards.
findings.limitations: Original 1807 Gazeta issue not found or examined; seventeen historical drying patios must NOT be equated with present four roofed library patios; phase plan needed.

findings.assertion: During the independence struggle the former factory was appropriated for military use and imprisonment; José María Morelos was confined there before his December 1815 execution, and the government converted it into an arms facility around 1816.
geographies: La Ciudadela / present Biblioteca de México
findings.source_locator: La Jornada 20 July 2014 lines 33-35; INAH ficha 12486 indexed text 'Hacia 1816'.
findings.limitations: Original confinement register, sentencing file, 1816 order and floor plan missing. Do not advertise a surviving Morelos prison cell without physical evidence.

findings.assertion: An 1843 calendar by Abraham López printed an image titled 'Pronunciamiento de la ciudadela de México' interpreting an August 31, 1841 political-military uprising at La Ciudadela. The calm lithographic scene is NOT a literal picture of the armed confrontation.
findings.source_locator: Esparza Liberal 2004 pp.12-14, fig.3 printed p.13, PDF page index 8 visually checked; La Jornada 2014 line 36 mentions an earlier 1840 revolt.
findings.limitations: Original 1843 calendar impression not viewed; UNAM researcher describes Valencia but published prose erroneously says 'Agustín Constanzó' for architecture, requiring name correction before approval.

findings.assertion: In February 1913 rebel troops used La Ciudadela as a fortified arsenal during the Decena Trágica; the building's function as a weapons depot explains its strategic importance, but exact cannon positions or present-day battle damage are unverified.
findings.source_locator: La Jornada 20 July 2014 line 37; institution catalog building history; prior project Decena Trágica chapter audit exists.
findings.limitations: Need independent February 1913 primary map/eyewitness record for precise positions; do not conflate Palacio Nacional engagement with La Ciudadela.

findings.assertion: The Mexican state allocated the former military complex for the Biblioteca de México in 1944 and inaugurated it in 1946 with José Vasconcelos directing; the historic building today serves a library rather than the adjacent Mercado de la Ciudadela.
findings.source_locator: Biblioteca de México official presentation, indexed; La Jornada 2014 lines 28-38; Arquine 2012 lines 20-23.
findings.limitations: No current access to interior courtyards guaranteed; building not interchangeable with adjacent crafts market or the separate Biblioteca Vasconcelos.

findings.assertion: Published architectural measurements describe the Ciudadela complex as a 168m-sided square with four 40m principal courtyards, and a later 1988 Abraham Zabludovsky intervention covering the courtyards; 2011 plans altered circulation and access.
findings.source_locator: Arquine 31 July 2012 lines 22-25; official Biblioteca de México page on interventions, indexed.
findings.limitations: These dimensions are from an architect's article not a field survey; 2011 plan as proposed versus as-built and accessible paths remain uncertain.

findings.assertion: By the mid-nineteenth century women making cigars in Mexico City encountered pressures from machine production, occupational deskilling, and collective resistance; the historical factory at La Ciudadela had already shifted to military use, so do not locate later cigarworkers' strikes inside it.
geographies: Mexico City / tobacco workplaces not geocoded
findings.source_locator: Teitelbaum and Gutiérrez 2009 Boletín Americanista 59 pp.265-288 institutional abstract; Ros 1985 Historias 10 pp.51-64 indexed abstract.
findings.limitations: Full texts, factory-specific addresses and labor-action dates not read; labor continuity is thematic, not proof of geographic/site continuity.

findings.assertion: Architect attribution needs an explicit conflict record: INAH's indexed catalog and other architectural histories name engineer Miguel Constanzó, whereas Esparza Liberal's 2004 PDF, printed p.13, calls the builder 'Agustín Constanzó'; do not silently reconcile divergent names.
findings.source_locator: INAH ficha 12486 indexed history vs UNAM Anales IIE 84 p.13 PDF visual screenshot; La Jornada 20 July 2014 line 31.
findings.limitations: Likely authorial slip but unproven; requires Spanish academy commission, original plan signature or authenticated biography before editorial resolution.
